# How a release reaches the package server

This page is for developers who publish packages, and for anyone who wants to know how a change to a site package
gets to new installations. It describes the process 7x follows, step by step, and the checks that belong to each
step. The same process works for a package server of your own.

1. [The process in one table](#the-process-in-one-table)
2. [Step 1: change the source and commit](#step-1-change-the-source-and-commit)

4. [Step 3: compare](#step-3-compare)
5. [Step 4: copy into the release folder](#step-4-copy-into-the-release-folder)

## The process in one table

| Step | Where | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Change and commit | the source repository ([The source repositories](the-source-repositories.md)) | the change is recorded in the package's folder |
| 2. Build | `packages/build.sh` in that repository | one `<name>.ezpkg` per folder |
| 3. Compare | your working copy | you know exactly what changed in the archive |
| 4. Copy | the package server repository, `exponential/6.0/<version>/` | the new `.ezpkg` replaces the old one |
| 5. Index | `exponential/6.0/<version>/index.xml` | changed only when a package is new, renamed or gets a new version or summary |
| 6. Commit and push | the package server repository, branch `master` | GitHub Pages republishes the site |

## Step 1: change the source and commit

Make the change in the unpacked package folder, for example `packages/sevenx_multisite/settings/` of
`sevenx-ezpackage`. Commit it there first, so the source and the archive never disagree. Use a message that names the
package and says what changes for an installation:

```text
Updated: The installer of the sevenx_site package activates ezownerchange, so changing the owner of content is available in a new installation
```

If the change touches `package.xml`, check it first: `xmllint --noout packages/<name>/package.xml`
([Validating a package before publishing](../requirements/validating-a-package-before-publishing.md)).

## Step 2: build the archives

```bash
cd packages
./build.sh
```

`build.sh` packs every folder of `packages/` with `tar -zcf ../<folder>.ezpkg`, leaving out version control folders,
editor and operating system leftovers and `node_modules` (the list is in the script and in
[The source repositories](the-source-repositories.md#the-scripts)). The `.ezpkg` files are written next to the
folders. Repositories without `build.sh` use `bin/pack.sh --output-dir=<dir>`.
See [Rebuilding with build.sh](../your-own/rebuilding-with-build-sh.md).

## Step 3: compare

Before anything is copied, compare the new archive with the one on the server:

```bash
# file lists, old and new
curl -s https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/sevenx_site.ezpkg | tar -tzf - | sort > old.txt
tar -tzf sevenx_site.ezpkg | sort > new.txt
diff old.txt new.txt

# a single file, old and new
curl -s https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/sevenx_site.ezpkg | tar -xzOf - package.xml > old-package.xml
tar -xzOf sevenx_site.ezpkg package.xml | diff old-package.xml -
```

Check that:

- [ ] only the files you meant to change differ;
- [ ] no `.git`, `.DS_Store`, editor backup or other stray file is in the list;
- [ ] `package.xml` is at the top of the archive, not inside a folder;
- [ ] the file still starts with the gzip signature (`file sevenx_site.ezpkg` says "gzip compressed data").

Write the comparison files to a working folder of your own, not to a shared temporary folder.

## Step 4: copy into the release folder

Copy the `.ezpkg` into the package server repository, into the folder of the release it belongs to:

```bash
cp sevenx_site.ezpkg <package-server-clone>/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/
```

A fix to a released package **replaces the file in place**: the same name, the same folder, the same URL. Every
installation that reads that folder gets the fixed file from then on. The earlier file stays in the Git history only.

## Step 5: update index.xml

The index changes only when:

- a package is added (a new `<package>` entry, and for a site package a thumbnail in `thumbnails/`);
- a package is renamed or removed;
- the `version`, `summary` or `description` of a site package should read differently in the setup wizard.

A fix to an existing package needs no change to the index. After an edit, check the file with `xmllint --noout` and
check every `url` ([The index.xml format](the-index-xml-format.md#checking-an-index)).

## Step 6: commit and push

Commit in the package server repository with the same kind of message, naming the package:

```text
Updated: The sevenx_site package's installer activates ezownerchange
```

Push to `master`. The workflow builds the directory listings and deploys the site
([The package server on GitHub](the-package-server-on-github.md#from-push-to-web-site)). Then:

- [ ] wait for the run under **Actions** to finish;
- [ ] fetch the file from the server and compare its checksum with yours (`sha256sum`);
- [ ] remember that the server sends `Cache-Control: max-age=600`: a cache may hand out the old file for up to ten
      minutes;
- [ ] install once from the server into a sandbox ([Testing in a sandbox](../your-own/testing-in-a-sandbox.md)).

> **Note**
> Since 2026-10-12 deployments run one at a time; pushes in quick succession wait for each other instead of failing.
> Pushing one commit per package is fine.

## A new release folder

For a new Exponential release, the history shows this pattern (6.0.14 on 2026-06-05, 6.0.15 on 2026-08-07):

1. Create `exponential/6.0/<new version>/` with all its packages, `index.xml` and `thumbnails/`.
2. Make sure every `url` and `thumbnail_url` in the new `index.xml` names the new folder. Right after the 6.0.15
   import, a commit titled "Bugfix for new package urls" corrected the entries of `sevenx_multisite` and
   `sevenx_multisite_clean`.
3. Push, and check the folder in a browser.
4. In the kernel, point `settings/package.ini [RepositorySettings] RemotePackagesIndexURL` at the new folder, in the
   release that should use it ([Package server settings](package-server-settings.md)).

Older folders stay, so installations of older releases keep working.

## An example from the history

On 2026-10-15 one change went through both repositories:

| Repository | Commit |
|---|---|
| `sevenx-ezpackage` | "Updated: The installer of the sevenx_site package activates ezownerchange, so changing the owner of content is available in a new installation" (one PHP file in `packages/sevenx_site/settings/`, three lines) |
| `exponential.packages.exponential.earth` | "Updated: The sevenx_site package's installer activates ezownerchange" (`exponential/6.0/6.0.15/sevenx_site.ezpkg`, 79,228 to 79,291 bytes) |
